text: When we look to the individuals of the same variety or sub-variety of our older cultivated plants and animals, one of the first points which strikes us, is, that they generally differ much more from each other, than do the individuals of any one species or variety in a state of nature. When, for instance, we compare the Han Chinese with the Anglo-Saxon, or the Negro with the European, or again the horse with the donkey, or the dog with the wolf, we find that the differences are much greater than those between the individuals of the same species in a state of nature.

When we look to the individuals of the same variety or sub-variety of our older cultivated plants and animals, one of the first points which strikes us,
Is,
That they generally differ much more from each other,
Than do the individuals of any one species or variety in a state of nature.
When, for instance, we compare the Han Chinese with the Anglo-Saxon,
Or the Negro with the European,
Or again the horse with the donkey,
Or the dog with the wolf,
We find that the differences are much greater than those between the individuals of the same species in a state of nature.
